review.notes: Reviewed complete actual catalog union: 7 scalar functions, supported_encodings table plus same-named table-function alias, 0 views. Eight logical objects; no hidden/authenticated/write APIs omitted. The interfaces have identical 8 logical names and signatures. Current source changes the transcode implementation for UTF-16LE/BE output and rejects replacement encoding; those paths are outside the three selected export codecs. A real SQL probe returns 68C3A9 for transcode(hé,UTF-16LE) on release and 6800E900 on current source. Metadata/examples and tests also changed; other demonstrated decoding, detection, repair and legacy/UTF-8 export logic is unchanged. Interface coverage does not claim implementation equivalence or exhaustive codec tests.

review.purpose: Establish a supported comparison population before exporting text.
review.finding: The actual catalog lists 40 encoding labels. Three selected labels drive the export cross join and explicit preflight. Recognized labels do not prove every release encoder works; UTF-16 export is excluded with a documented release/current discrepancy.

review.purpose: Compare guesses against independently specified source encodings and intended text.
review.finding: The detector-derived decoded text matches 3/4 known fixtures; the short Japanese sample is misidentified. This small constructed set is not a population accuracy estimate.

review.purpose: Determine whether a clean decode score establishes correct interpretation.
review.finding: The mismatched Japanese guess still has a proxy of 1.0. This score measures decode cleanliness, not calibrated confidence in original intent; empty and missing input have NULL detection evidence.

review.purpose: Separate byte validity from successful text recovery and missing evidence.
review.finding: Only 1/4 source payloads are valid UTF-8, though all four decode using their declared labels. Empty bytes are valid UTF-8 without detection evidence; missing bytes return NULL; FF is invalid and explicit UTF-8 decoding emits U+FFFD.

review.purpose: Evaluate automatic decoding without allowing the detector to define its own ground truth.
review.finding: Automatic decoded text disagrees with independently supplied Japanese text despite a cleanliness proxy of 1.0. Explicit provenance and expected text distinguish clean output from correct interpretation.

review.purpose: Recover known fixture text using independent source labels and verify exported bytes with their declared destinations.
review.finding: Declared source decoding recovers every fixture, including UTF-16LE BOM stripping. Eight relationship checks pass; explicit labels alone still do not guarantee byte validity, as the lossy UTF-8 control demonstrates.

review.purpose: Assess a repair proposal against both known corruption and intentional literal characters.
review.finding: The heuristic changes 2/3 examples and 1/3 proposals disagrees with stated intent. The intentional literal sequence shows why repair is reviewable, not an automatic normalization rule.

review.purpose: Choose an export encoding based on exact text preservation before comparing byte counts.
review.finding: Windows-1252 preserves 2/4 strings and totals 42 bytes; changing only destination to UTF-8 preserves 4/4 and totals 23 bytes. Accent bytes grow 4→5 while Japanese shrinks 24→9. Legacy numeric references remain literal text. The exercised three codecs are unchanged in current source; UTF-16/replacement fixes are separate documented behavior drift.
